title: Run it as a project, not as four private chats
desc: The Projects group in the sidebar and the rail behind it: three roles, team chats versus shared AI chats, project memory, and what deleting a project takes with it.
learningGoal: After this lesson you can create a project, give it instructions for the AI, invite a colleague as Editor or Viewer, tell a team chat from a shared AI chat and what sharing does to its encryption, and find the project's own memory.

steps.title: Four people, four private chats, one job
steps.bodyMd:
Marieke is projectleider at **Van Dijk Groep**, the sixty-person installation firm near Zwolle. She is preparing a tender for a housing renovation with three colleagues, and right now the job lives in four separate heads: Bas has the supplier prices in his chat history, Karin has the drawings in a notebook only she can open, and Marieke keeps re-pasting the same house style into every prompt.

Nothing there is broken. It is just that a conversation in Bee Flow belongs to one person by default, and so does almost everything else.

A **project** is the exception. It is a named workspace that several colleagues open on the same footing: team chats, tasks, documents, notebooks and meeting notes, the files and knowledge bases the answers should draw on, and a set of instructions that every AI chat inside it follows. Projects are part of the Enterprise edition, so the row only appears if your organisation has it.

steps.title: The part of the sidebar you have scrolled past
steps.body: This is the top of the sidebar. Once you have a project, a group headed Projects sits lower down: a plus titled New Project, a row per project (tagged shared if a colleague owns it; hover it for a plus that starts a chat there) and All projects. Until then it is one New Project row. Neither shows in Simple Mode. The list page adds search, sorting and the filters All, Mine and Shared with me.

steps.title: One rail, ten sections
steps.bodyMd:
Open a project and a rail runs down its left side, under the project's name and your role:

- **Collaborate** — **Overview** first: start a conversation, see what changed since your last visit, add work, and a summary of the instructions, members and knowledge. Then **Chats** (team chats and AI chats in the project), **Tasks**, and **Meetings** for recorded or uploaded meetings with their notes.
- **Content** — **Documents** to write together, **Notebooks**, and **Knowledge**: the files, knowledge bases and project memory every chat can draw on.
- **Manage** — **Members**, **Activity**, and **Settings**: name, description, icon and colour, the AI's instructions, and at the bottom delete (owner) or leave (everyone else).

Notebooks is left out of the rail for anyone whose plan or role does not include notebooks.

**Instructions for the AI**, under Settings, are the quiet workhorse: *"Added to every AI chat in this project: tone, context, what to keep in mind."* The house style gets written once instead of pasted four times a day.

steps.title: Send each request to its section
steps.instruction: Six things the tender team needs. Match each to the section of the project's rail that owns it.

pairs.left: "Bas should be able to open the two conversations we are working from."
pairs.note: Chats lists every conversation of the project: team chats, AI chats members shared, and your own private ones filed here. The filter offers All, Unread, Shared and Private.

pairs.left: "Answers here should quote our own tender documents, not the open web."
pairs.note: Knowledge holds the files uploaded into the project (up to 20 MB each) and the linked knowledge bases. Chats in this project answer from both.

pairs.left: "Marieke and Bas need to write the tender letter together."
pairs.note: Documents is for writing together: everyone in the project can read a document and editors can write in it. New document starts one; Add existing files in one of your own.

pairs.left: "Karin wants to know who changed her role last week."
pairs.note: Activity is the project's log: who invited whom as which role, who changed whose role, who left, who updated the instructions for the AI, which AI chats were shared or made private again. It can be filtered by Chats, Content, People or Project.

pairs.left: "Every answer in this project should be in Dutch, with prices ex VAT."
pairs.note: A standing rule for the AI goes in Instructions for the AI on Settings, which is added to every AI chat in the project. A fact the team keeps repeating fits project memory on Knowledge instead.

pairs.left: "Tuesday's site meeting with the supplier should be kept with the job, action items and all."
pairs.note: Meetings takes a recording or an upload (Record or upload) and keeps its transcript, summary and action items in the project. Every member can read them; only the person who recorded a meeting can change it.

steps.title: Owner, Editor, Viewer — and who may hand out which
steps.bodyMd:
On **Members** the owner gets an **Invite people** form: choose **Person** or **Group**, pick who, then a role. The role dropdown offers exactly two, **Editor** and **Viewer**, with Viewer preselected. Below the list, *What each role can do* spells them out:

- **Owner** — *"Everything an editor can, plus managing members and deleting the project."*
- **Editor** — *"Starts chats, manages tasks and content, and changes project and AI settings."*
- **Viewer** — *"Reads everything in the project, changes nothing."*

**Owner** is not on the invite list. It is whoever created the project, and only the owner sees the role dropdown and the remove button beside each member. Everyone else sees a role label, and on their own row a **Leave** button, which Activity records as leaving rather than being removed.

A Viewer really changes nothing: in a team chat they read *"You can read this chat. Only editors can post in it."* The buttons are hidden rather than shown and refused, because the server would refuse them anyway.

steps.question: Marieke wants Bas to link a knowledge base and adjust the project's instructions for the AI, but she does not want him inviting the rest of the office. Which role does she pick when she invites him?

choices.label: Viewer
choices.feedback: A Viewer reads everything in the project and changes nothing: no linking on Knowledge, no saving on Settings, not even a post in a team chat.

choices.label: Owner
choices.feedback: Owner is not on offer when inviting: the role dropdown holds Editor and Viewer only. The owner is whoever created the project, and that role is exactly the one that manages members and can delete the project.

choices.label: Editor, and she also turns on Remember useful facts from chats so he can write to project memory
choices.feedback: Two unrelated things. That toggle lets the AI save facts from chats on its own; adding, changing and removing project memory entries by hand is already an editor's right without it.

steps.explanation: Editor is the working role: start chats, manage tasks and content, change the project and AI settings, write project memory. Inviting people, changing roles, removing members and deleting the project stay with the owner.

steps.title: How a chat becomes the team's
steps.bodyMd:
A project holds two kinds of chat, and they start out differently.

**New chat** on Chats, or *Start a conversation* on Overview, opens a **team chat**: *"Everyone in this project can read along. Mention @AI when you want its help."* It starts on **On mention**, and **When the AI answers** at the top of the chat can change that.

An **AI chat** you start with the plus beside the project in the sidebar uses the project's instructions and knowledge, but it is listed on Chats as *Private: only you can see it*. To bring the team in, click **Share with members** on its row (the sidebar's ⋯ menu calls it **Share with project**). The confirmation is worth reading: *"Every member can then read it, and editors can continue it. It is encrypted with the project key instead of your own; your other chats stay private."*

That is literal: sharing re-encrypts the messages on the spot, and **Stop sharing** re-keys them back to you. Only a chat's owner can do either — on the zero-knowledge tier the key for the private version exists only while its owner is signed in.

steps.question: Marieke shares her private supplier AI chat with the tender project. What actually happens to that conversation?

choices.label: Its messages are re-encrypted at that moment with the project key instead of hers, so every member can read it and editors can continue it — and Stop sharing re-keys it back to her.
Nothing changes about the encryption; the project simply links to the conversation.
choices.feedback: It cannot stay as it was. A private chat is sealed with its owner's key, which no colleague holds — sharing has to re-key it, or no member could open it.

choices.label: A copy is placed in the project and the original stays private.
choices.feedback: There is no copy. It is the same conversation, now readable by the project — which is why Stop sharing makes it private again rather than deleting a duplicate.

choices.label: It becomes readable to Editors only, until Marieke grants each Viewer a key.
choices.feedback: There is no per-member key handout. Every member can read a shared chat; the Editor role decides who may continue it, not who may read it.

steps.explanation: Sharing is a re-key, not a link. It is the one moment a private AI chat stops being sealed to you alone — so decide before you share, and remember that only its owner can share it or take it back. Team chats need no sharing: they belong to the project from the first message.

steps.title: Project memory, with names on the entries
steps.bodyMd:
You already have a personal memory. A project keeps a separate one, at the bottom of **Knowledge** under **Project memory**: *"What the assistant remembers for this project, shared by every member. Editors can add, change and remove entries."* Each entry shows *by* whoever put it there, and an entry added by hand is an **Instruction, Project, Fact** or **Context**.

Two things to set straight before the team leans on it:

- It is **shared, not private**. Every member reads it; a Viewer gets no **Add memory** button.
- It is **quiet until you switch it on**. **Remember useful facts from chats**, under *AI in this project* on Settings, is off by default: *"The AI saves facts from chats in this project as project memory, so later chats can use them. Review them under Knowledge."* Until then the empty pool reads *"Automatic memory is off. Editors can add shared project facts here."*

Overview's *About this project* shows at a glance whether project memory is On or Off.

steps.title: Your turn: write the project's instructions for the AI
steps.instruction: Write the Instructions for the AI for Marieke's tender project — the text that goes under AI in this project on Settings and is added to every AI chat in the project. Three to five sentences. Make them standing rules the assistant should follow every time (language, tone, units, what to always include, what never to do), not a task for today. Keep customer names, addresses and account numbers out of it: every member of the project can read this text.
steps.placeholder: e.g. Answer in Dutch unless the question is in English. All prices are ex VAT in euros, and every quotation must name a delivery period. Never promise an installation date without a source in the project's knowledge bases…

steps.title: Remove, stop sharing, delete: three different exits
steps.bodyMd:
This is where people trip, because several controls all sound like undo.

- On **Documents**, **Notebooks** and **Meetings**, **Remove from project** takes an item out without deleting it: *"stays with its owner. Members of this project will no longer see it."* The button shows for the item's owner and for the project owner; a Viewer never sees it. On **Knowledge**, **Unlink** stops chats searching a knowledge base without changing the base itself.
- For an AI chat, **Stop sharing** makes it private again but leaves it filed in the project; **Remove from project** in the sidebar's ⋯ menu un-files it; only **Delete** deletes it. Deleting a team chat removes its messages for everyone.
- At the bottom of **Settings**, the owner's **Delete this project** asks for the project's name and warns: *"Team chats are deleted with it. Documents, notebooks, meetings and private chats stay with the people who made them. Chats shared with the project must be made private first."* Everyone else sees **Leave this project** there instead.

steps.question: The tender is lost. Marieke opens Settings and clicks Delete this project. Which outcome should she expect?

choices.label: Team chats, the member list, the activity history and project memory are deleted; documents, notebooks, meetings and private chats stay with the people who made them.
Everything the team put in the project is deleted with it, documents and meetings included.
choices.feedback: The warning says the opposite before you confirm: documents, notebooks, meetings and private chats stay with the people who made them, as standalone items.

choices.label: Nothing happens until every member has left the project first.
choices.feedback: Members do not need to leave. What does block the delete is an AI chat still shared with the project: its owner has to make it private first, because a shared chat cannot outlive its project.

choices.label: Bas can undo it, because he is an Editor.
choices.feedback: Bas never saw the button: Delete this project is only shown to the owner, and editors see Leave this project instead. There is no undo — which is why it asks for the project's name first.

steps.explanation: Deleting a project unpicks the collaboration, not people's own work. What disappears is what only existed because the project existed: its team chats, membership, activity history and project memory.

steps.title: Build one — we'll verify it
steps.instruction: In the sidebar, click the plus beside the Projects heading (or the New Project row if you have none yet), name the project — Marieke would use the job name — and click Create project. Open Settings in the project's rail, paste the instructions you just wrote into Instructions for the AI and click Save. Then open Members and invite one colleague as Viewer or Editor.

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
- **Set a job up as a project.** New Project in the sidebar, then Settings for the name, the colour and the Instructions for the AI — which reach every AI chat in the project without anyone pasting them.
- **Put people on the right rung.** The owner invites, changes roles and deletes; an Editor starts chats and manages tasks, content and settings; a Viewer reads everything and changes nothing.
- **Share with your eyes open.** A team chat belongs to the project from the start. A private AI chat only joins when its owner clicks Share with members, which re-encrypts it with the project key; Stop sharing re-keys it back.

One habit to take with you: project memory on Knowledge is a team noticeboard, not a private notebook. Put conventions there, keep customer details out of it — and turn on Remember useful facts from chats only when you want the project to start learning on its own.

ex-projects-shared-workspace-instruction.title: Instructions for the AI in a shared project
ex-projects-shared-workspace-instruction.task: Write three to five sentences of Instructions for the AI for a tender project at Van Dijk Groep — standing rules added to every AI chat in the project, with no personal or customer data in them.
criteria: Reads as standing rules that apply to every chat in the project (language, tone, units, format, what to always include or never do), not as a one-off task or a question.
At least two concrete, checkable rules rather than vague ambition — for example a language, a currency or VAT convention, a required element in every quotation, or a source requirement.
Fits a shared workspace: written for the whole team, in the second person to the assistant, not as personal preferences about one user.
Contains no customer names, addresses, e-mail addresses, phone numbers or account numbers — nothing that should not be read by every member of the project.
ex-projects-shared-workspace-instruction.guidance: Do not pass a single sentence, a request phrased as a task for today ('write the tender letter'), or text that merely describes the project without instructing the assistant. Do not pass anything containing a real-looking personal detail, even as an example. A learner who writes short, plain, specific rules should pass; polish and length are not the point.

practiceTopic.title: Projects: the shared workspace
practiceTopic.summary: How a project's rail, three roles, team and shared AI chats, project memory and delete fit together for a team working on one job.
facts: A project's rail has three groups: Collaborate (Overview, Chats, Tasks, Meetings), Content (Documents, Notebooks, Knowledge) and Manage (Members, Activity, Settings); Notebooks is left out for anyone whose plan or role does not include notebooks.

Settings holds About this project (name, description, icon, colour) and AI in this project: Instructions for the AI, added to every AI chat in the project, and the toggle Remember useful facts from chats, which is off by default.

The Invite people form on Members offers two roles, Editor and Viewer, with Viewer preselected. Only the owner invites, changes roles or removes members; a Viewer reads everything in the project and changes nothing.
New chat on the Chats tab starts a team chat every member can read; the AI answers when someone mentions @AI, and viewers can read but not post.

An AI chat filed in a project stays private until its owner clicks Share with members (Share with project in the sidebar menu): it is re-encrypted with the project key, every member can read it and editors can continue it; Stop sharing re-keys it back.
Project memory sits on the Knowledge tab next to Files and Knowledge bases; every member sees it, editors add, change and remove entries, and each entry names who added it.
Remove from project on Documents, Notebooks and Meetings takes an item out without deleting it: it stays with its owner. It is offered to the item's owner and the project owner.

Delete this project (owner only, at the bottom of Settings) deletes team chats, members, activity and project memory, keeps documents, notebooks, meetings and private chats with their makers, and is refused while chats are still shared with the project.

actionChecks.label: Create a project of your own
actionChecks.hint: Sidebar → New Project, name it and click Create project; then fill in Instructions for the AI on the project's Settings and save.

endpoints.returns: array of project rows with id, name, description, customInstructions, knowledgeBaseIds, color, icon, ownerId, extractMemories and permission ('owner'/'editor'/'viewer')

criteria.label: A project you own exists
criteria.hint: Click New Project in the sidebar, give it a name and click Create project — the project you create is yours. The instructions you type on Settings are stored inside the project, where this check cannot look.
criteria.rule: GET /api/projects → at least one row whose ownerId is the learner (rows check; shared projects carry someone else’s ownerId)
